description: This course covers C++ programming fundamentals with an emphasis on object-oriented programming principles. Topics include classes and objects; inheritance, polymorphism, and encapsulation; STL containers and algorithms; memory management with smart pointers; exception handling; templates; and standard library facilities. The course also explores design patterns such as Singleton, Factory, and Observer; file I/O operations; and integration with modern C++ standards (C++17 and C++20). Students will implement real-world applications using these concepts.

clos.text: Define C++ syntax and semantics for object-oriented programming constructs such as classes, objects, inheritance, and polymorphism.
Describe the memory management mechanisms in C++ including stack, heap, and smart pointers.
Explain the principles of design patterns such as Singleton, Factory, and Observer and their implementation in C++.
Apply C++ STL containers and algorithms to solve complex data manipulation problems.
Implement a complete software application using object-oriented principles and modern C++ standards.
